Yes: DACT proposes continual tokenization that updates item identifiers under drift while trying to preserve prior alignment with the generative recommender [5]. It uses a drift identification module plus hierarchical code reassignment to change token sequences only where needed, which is aimed at handling evolving user-behavior patterns without fully retraining the whole system [5].

If you want a more direct match on preserving learned mappings during updates, another strong fit is the topology-preserving update strategy that says to insert new items, freeze old items, and warm-start when possible, because changing learned SIDs hurts retrieval quality [1].
